body_excerpt: Handing Carmen three terrorist heads pays out $20,000 instead of $30,000. One or two heads pay correctly; three loses exactly one head's bounty. The reporter's own guess — that $20,000 is a per-slot money limit — is **correct**, and the slot is `MAX_MONEY_PER_SLOT`. ## Reproducing 1. Start the quest, meet Carmen, and collect at least three terrorist heads. 2. Give the heads to Carmen and change sector (the payout happens on the sector change). 3. Talk to Carmen in C13 to collect. | Heads | Owed | Player receives | Lost | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | $10,000 | $10,000 | — | | 2 | $20,000 | $20,000 | — | | 3 | $30,000 | **$20,000** | $10,000 | | 4 | $40,000 | **$20,000** | $20,000 | One and two heads fit in a single pocket stack, which is why the bug only appears at three. ## Root cause: the bounty is physical money objects, not an amount The payout is not a transaction. `src/game/Strategic/Strategic_Event_Handler.cc:813-831` credits the **profile** a scalar: ```cpp if (gMercProfiles[ CARMEN ].bNPCData2 > 0) { if (gMercProfiles[ CARMEN ].uiMoney < 10000) uiAmount = 0; else uiAmount = gMercProfiles[ CARMEN ].uiMoney; uiAmount += 10000 * gMercProfiles[ CARMEN ].bNPCData2; // $10k per head SetMoneyInSoldierProfile( CARMEN, uiAmount ); gMercProfiles[ CARMEN ].bNPCData2 = 0; ... } ``` So 3 heads is correctly recorded as $30,000. Nothing is lost here. The money becomes objects when Carmen is spawned into a sector. `CopyProfileItems` (`src/game/Tactical/Soldier_Create.cc:2059-2069`) splits the scalar into pocket-sized stacks: ```cpp for (UINT32 money_left = p.uiMoney; money_left > 0;) { INT8 const slot_id = FindEmptySlotWithin(&s, POCK1POS, POCK12POS); if (slot_id == NO_SLOT) break; UINT32 const slot_limit = MoneySlotLimit(slot_id); UINT32 const slot_amount = std::min(money_left, slot_limit); CreateMoney(slot_amount, slot); money_left -= slot_amount; } ``` `MoneySlotLimit` (`src/game/Tactical/Items.cc:325-335`) caps a stack at `MAX_MONEY_PER_SLOT` = **20000** (`src/game/Tactical…

body_excerpt: 60## Architecture & Feature Requirement We need to expand the UltimateAI action subsystem by introducing a headless `LibreOfficeAutomationTool` module. This tool will run safely inside containerized or local server-side environments to convert, manipulate, and generate enterprise documents (DOCX, XLSX, PDF) on behalf of AI requests. ### Core Acceptance Criteria: 1. **Zero-Trust Hard Boundary Gatekeeper:** Enforce a hard budget constraint of **$150 maximum compute allocation limits** per session window to prevent resource exploitation or billing leaks. 2. **Strict Multi-Payload Size Defense:** Reject individual input payloads exceeding **5MB** using explicit `StandardCharsets.UTF_8` evaluation. 3. **Path Protection:** Restrict document generation strictly inside the managed directory base path (`ultimate-managed-workspaces`). 4. **Parallel Stream Harvesting:** Read Process output (stdout/stderr) via independent daemon runner threads to eliminate OS pipe deadlocks. 5. **Auto-Teardown Mechanism:** Ensure all compiled or converted files are purged from volatile server storage in a `finally` block post-execution. ###Labels `bounty`, `security`, `feature`, `good first issue` `Help needed`

body_excerpt: Currently, when [using Trovu from its PWA](https://trovu.net/docs/users/integration/#pwa-progressive-web-app), target URLs are opened within the PWA. Instead, they shall - open in the default browser of the device, if no app is linked to this URL (e.g. URLs to Google shall open in Chrome or Firefox or whatever the default browser is) - open in the matching app (e.g. links to Google Maps or Youtube shall open in these apps, if they are installed). I assume this can be solved just with the right settings inside the PWA configuration. **Edit 2026-06-17:** Please note [this comment](https://github.com/trovu/trovu/issues/329#issuecomment-2062401881 ) stating that it might be technically impossible to solve this (at the moment) due to how PWAs are handled. **Edit 2026-05-23:** By now, I am receiving a new PR almost every day. All of them claim to solve the problem, yet when testing, *none of them have worked so far*. This is very frustrating. Even more frustrating is that when I comment that it's not working, I often get very wordy replies, new commits, and promises that "now it's working" – and it still isn't. It is very likely that those comments are written by AI. I don't mind if you use AI for coding, or if you use AI to fix the grammar of your comments. But in the comments, I want to talk to a human. Therefore, for me to consider any further PRs, please provide the following: ### Please include in the comment of your pull request: * A video recorded on an Android device, showing: * You open the Trovu PWA. * You send the query `g`. - The target URL (Google) opens **outside the PWA**, in the installed browser. It must be clearly visible that it is a browser, meaning: - There is an address bar showing the URL. - There is a tab switcher button (in Chrome, it's the square with a number in it). * The following statement: `I am a human who is writing this comment, not an AI.` Again, I don't mind if you code with AI. But in the comments, I want to talk to a human.
